abstract: Accumulation of senescent cells is increasingly viewed as a significant contributor to aging and age-related diseases. To date, the elimination of senescent cells through small molecule senolytic agents has largely relied on a limited number of repurposed agents, often leveraged from previous oncological applications. Here, we describe a CRISPR-based, genome-wide, synthetic lethal screen for senescent cells. From this screen, we identify a number of genes whose deletion appears to be well tolerated in normal proliferating cells, but whose deletion is lethal in the context of senescence. We further characterize one promising candidate gene encoding the ER-resident protein PARP16. Knockdown of PARP16 does not affect the viability of mouse or human cells but results in the death of a wide range of senescent cells. Furthermore, two distinct small molecule PARP16 inhibitors have little effect of normal cell growth but result in the selective death of senescent cells in culture and in freshly isolated human donor lung tissue explants. Together, these results demonstrate a rational strategy to identify novel senolytic therapies that could have potential applications for a wide range of age-related conditions.

title: A genome-wide senescence synthetic lethality screen identifies PARP16 as a senolytic target.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic inflammatory diseases involve persistent interactions between immune signaling, tissue injury, and metabolic dysfunction. Immunometabolism provides a framework for understanding how metabolic pathways regulate immune-cell activation and inflammatory persistence.
METHODS: This narrative review examines the roles of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism in chronic inflammation. It evaluates their regulation by AMPK, mTOR, HIF-1α, NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and NLRP3 across rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, airway diseases, cardiometabolic disorders, atherosclerosis, and neuroinflammation. Established pharmacological interventions and emerging drug-delivery, RNA-based, gene-editing, cellular, and microbiome-directed approaches are also discussed.
RESULTS: Metabolic reprogramming contributes to inflammatory activation and disease persistence through interconnected signaling networks. Although established therapies, including dimethyl fumarate, exert immunometabolic effects, these cannot be attributed exclusively to metabolic reprogramming. Most selective metabolic inhibitors and advanced therapeutic platforms remain experimental for chronic inflammatory indications. Major translational challenges include metabolic redundancy, tissue-specific responses, heterogeneous disease endotypes, insufficient target-engagement evidence, and potential impairment of protective immunity.
CONCLUSION: Targeting immunometabolic pathways represents a promising therapeutic strategy for chronic inflammatory diseases. However, clinical translation requires mechanistic validation, patient stratification, reliable pharmacodynamic biomarkers, reproducible human tissue studies, and adequately powered clinical trials evaluating meaningful clinical outcome.

abstract: Androgen receptor (AR)-mediated transcription drives prostate cancer progression and remains a critical therapeutic target. AR activation by androgens triggers nuclear translocation, DNA binding at AR regulatory elements (AREs), and transcription initiation. This process involves co-factors such as FOXA1, epigenetic modifications, and three-dimensional (3D) chromatin interactions. However, the temporal coordination of these events during AR-mediated transcription remains poorly understood. Using a time-course androgen stimulation model in prostate cancer cells, we first integrated temporal multi-omics data within the MOFA+/MEFISTO framework, which identified three distinct temporal factors underlying AR-mediated transcriptional dynamics, and then used higher-resolution early time-course profiling to further explore the chromatin and transcriptional context of these temporal patterns. Our combined analyses revealed that rapid AR binding at gene promoters, as early as 5 min, is crucial for initiating nascent transcription of AR target genes. We found that H3K27 acetylation at flanking AREs, pre-marked by constitutive FOXA1 binding, occurs prior to AR recruitment. Additionally, androgen stimulation induced a temporal early shift in nascent transcription from MYC to AR target genes, associated with transient disruption of 3D chromatin interactions. Finally, we showed that CRISPR-mediated inhibition of AR-associated chromatin contacts suppresses distal linked target genes, demonstrating that dynamic genome architecture is functionally required for AR-driven transcription. Together these findings uncover the dynamic reorganization of 3D chromatin structure and transcription factor binding post-androgen stimulation, resulting in distinct temporal epigenomic states.

title: Androgen stimulation rapidly reorganizes temporal 3D genome and epigenome states to trigger AR-mediated transcription in prostate cancer.

abstract: Mitochondria are now recognized as central regulators of tumor biology, extending beyond their traditional role in bioenergetics to control cell survival, stress responses, immune signaling, and adaptation to therapeutic pressures. In cancers, mitochondrial plasticity encompasses, in particular, metabolic reprogramming, redox regulation, mitochondrial DNA signaling, mitochondrial dynamics, and quality control mechanisms, enabling tumor cells to adapt to a heterogeneous and challenging microenvironment. However, these alterations are not limited to malignant cells: they also influence the mitochondrial state and functions of various immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment. The reciprocal interactions between tumor and immune mitochondria, involving metabolic competition, mitochondrial-derived signals, and, more recently, intercellular mitochondrial transfer, can promote immune dysfunction and tumor escape. These mechanisms contribute to resistance to immunotherapies, particularly immune checkpoint blockade, as well as to resistance to certain chemotherapies and targeted therapies. This review integrates these mechanisms around a central concept: mitochondrial plasticity serves as a functional interface linking tumor adaptation, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance. We also examine mitochondrial vulnerabilities that could be exploited therapeutically, emphasizing the highly context-dependent nature of mitochondrial targeting and the need to preserve mitochondrial functions essential for antitumor immunity. Finally, we discuss mitochondrial heterogeneity, potential biomarkers, and emerging approaches based on single-cell, spatial, CRISPR, and multi-omics technologies, which could enable more precise identification of mitochondrial vulnerabilities and improved patient stratification. Together, these advances pave the way for a transition from nonspecific mitochondrial targeting to context-specific and precision mitochondrial immunotherapy.

title: Mitochondria in cancer: unravelling their role in resistance to therapies.

abstract: Ovarian cancer remains difficult to cure because disseminated peritoneal disease, heterogeneity, and resistance to platinum and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors limit treatment durability. Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors offer sustained transgene expression and capsid and regulatory cassette engineering, but translation is constrained by incomplete tumor-selective delivery, limited cargo capacity, host immunity, and heterogeneous tumor states. We examine AAV-mediated therapy in the context of recurrent and drug-resistant ovarian cancer. We discuss receptor retargeting, intraperitoneal versus systemic delivery, suicide genes, cytokines, genome editing, tumor suppressor restoration, and secreted antiangiogenic payloads. The most extensive ovarian AAV precedent concerns antiangiogenic and vascular-normalizing approaches; EpCAM-directed delivery and PD-L1-targeted AAV-CRISPR provide early evidence. FOLR1-targeted IL-12 efficacy and immune response findings derive from engineered MC38 colorectal tumors, with ovarian-cell targeting demonstrated separately. Studies do not establish restoration of platinum or PARP inhibitor sensitivity or any clinical benefit in resistant ovarian cancer. Chemotherapy combinations have preclinical support, whereas combinations with PARP inhibitors, checkpoint inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates remain hypotheses requiring direct testing. We outline biomarker-informed patient selection, immunological barriers to redosing, manufacturing and regulatory requirements, and a staged clinical development framework. Translation requires clinically representative resistant models and independent validation of delivery, pharmacodynamic activity, and safety before durable benefit can be inferred.

abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the therapeutic landscape of onco-hematology, evolving from historical allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) to modern chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T/NK cell therapies, bispecific antibodies, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Central to this immunological cross-talk is the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) system, which governs self/non-self-discrimination, alloreactivity, and tumor immune evasion across both classical allografts and novel adoptive cellular platforms. Facing hematological malignancies, ranging from acute leukemias and multiple myeloma to chronic leukemias and lymphomas, clinicians must overcome tumor immune escape while managing treatment-related toxicities and Graft-versus-Host Disease (GvHD). Advances in high-throughput molecular biology techniques, notably Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) and long-read sequencing, have become indispensable for high-resolution HLA matching, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and chimerism analysis. Furthermore, gene-editing strategies (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9) targeting TRAC, B2M, and CIITA, alongside HLA-E engineering and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology, are driving the development of universal "off-the-shelf" effector platforms that bypass classic HLA barriers. In this review, we provide a conceptual synthesis of immunotherapeutic paradigms in onco-hematology, highlighting the pivotal role of HLA biology and molecular diagnostics in shaping next-generation personalized cellular therapies.

title: Oncohematology in the Era of Immunotherapies: The Key Role of the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) Complex.

abstract: RICTOR, a core component of mTORC2, regulates cell survival, proliferation, and cytoskeletal organization. To dissect its role in epithelial cell biology, we generated ten clonal HEK-293T lines with frameshift deletions in the RICTOR gene using paired sgRNAs targeting exon 3. sgRNA efficiency was assessed by TIDE and T7E1 assays, and the two best sgRNAs were selected for deletion induction. Overall, 10 clonal lines with composite deletion were isolated. Complete loss of RICTOR mRNA in these clones was verified by RT-qPCR. Targeted qRT-PCR profiling revealed a consistent molecular signature: downregulation of some mTORC2-associated genes, compensatory upregulation of mTORC1 components (RPTOR, PRAS40) and PRR5, and increased ERK1/2 mRNA and, in most clones, increased ERK1/2 protein and p-ERK2. Proliferation was significantly slowed (doubling time increased nearly 50%, from 30 to 47 h). Scratch-wound assays demonstrated markedly reduced migration. Notably, RICTOR-KO cells formed compact multicellular aggregates instead of a dispersed monolayer, accompanied by upregulation of adhesion genes (CDH1, FLNA, FN1, ITGA5) and downregulation of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers (VIM, SNAI1, ZEB1). Our results establish HEK-293T RICTOR-KO as a valuable model to study mTORC2-dependent regulation of adhesion and migration, and highlight the interplay between mTOR and MAPK signaling in maintaining epithelial homeostasis. Potential therapeutic use of RICTOR-KO as an inhibitor of malignancy of solid tumors deserves further investigation.

abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) remains a major diagnostic challenge in healthcare-associated infections. Effective management requires clinicians to determine whether a positive result represents active infection, characterize resistance, and identify treatment options. This narrative review examines established and emerging CRAB diagnostic methods, their clinical applications, limitations, and potential to guide antimicrobial therapy. Molecular assays detect selected carbapenem-resistance determinants; however, their target range limits interpretation, and gene detection alone cannot establish the full susceptibility profile. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) remains essential for assessing isolate-specific activity. Method-dependent uncertainty is especially important for agents such as cefiderocol and colistin. Whole-genome sequencing supports resistance analysis, strain characterization, and outbreak investigation. Metagenomic sequencing, CRISPR-based assays, laboratory automation, and artificial intelligence offer additional capabilities, although their role in routine CRAB management is not established. Distinguishing active infection from colonization remains difficult, particularly with respiratory and wound specimens. Evidence that rapid diagnostic pathways improve outcomes specifically in CRAB infection remains limited; findings from broader bloodstream-infection populations cannot be generalized to every CRAB presentation. Future multicenter studies should validate integrated diagnostic-management pathways and assess their effects on treatment decisions and patient outcomes. Integrating clinical assessment with reliable organism identification and susceptibility testing can support timely, targeted treatment while minimizing unnecessary antimicrobial exposure when CRAB detection represents colonization without evidence of active infection.

title: From Detection to Decision: Linking Microbiological Diagnostics to the Clinical Management of Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Infection.

abstract: Hendra virus (HeV) is a zoonotic pathogen that can cause severe disease in humans. Because early symptoms are nonspecific and no licensed human vaccine or specific antiviral treatment is available, rapid testing may support timely clinical management. We developed an amplification-free CRISPR-field-effect transistor (CRISPR-FET) assay for HeV RNA. This study reports a novel amplification-free nucleic acid detection platform (CRISPR-FET) that integrates the specific collateral cleavage activity of CRISPR/Cas13a with the sensitive transduction capability of FETs. The CRISPR-FET platform achieves sensitive detection of Hendra virus nucleic acids with a limit of detection as low as 101 copies/μL (Ct value 33.0), eliminating the need for target nucleic acid preamplification and significantly streamlining the diagnostic process. To validate the specificity and reliability of this approach, we conducted cross-reactivity tests using eight RNA viruses with clinically similar symptoms and evaluated detection performance with 26 simulated clinical samples. However, the current study was performed using simulated rather than authentic clinical specimens, and the assay provides qualitative rather than quantitative results. Further validation with a larger number of clinical samples are required before clinical application.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Messenger RNA therapeutics enable rapid, transient protein expression without risk of genomic integration, but their delivery to post-mitotic neurons remains challenging. Here, we present a neuron-targeted liposomal platform designed to enhance mRNA delivery efficiency in neurons.
METHODS: We engineered DOTAP: DOPE liposomes to promote nucleic acid loading, stability, and endosomal escape, incorporated PEGylation to improve biocompatibility and circulation, and functionalized the liposome surface with a rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG)-derived peptide for neuronal targeting. We assessed particle size and surface charge, mRNA encapsulation/loading across different lipid: mRNA ratios, cytotoxicity in HEK293T cells as a function of cationic lipid content and PEGylation, and transfection performance in HEK293T cells and primary neurons, benchmarking against a commercial transfection reagent, with functional mRNA delivery further demonstrated in midbrain organoids following microinjection.
RESULTS: The system enabled efficient mRNA encapsulation, maintained favorable particle size and surface charge characteristics, and supported low cytotoxicity. Across formulations, mRNA loading increased with lipid: mRNA ratio, with only modest reductions following PEGylation. In HEK293T cells, higher cationic lipid content increased its toxicity, whereas PEGylation reduced membrane interactions and improved tolerability. Transfection studies identified the 50:10 DOTAP: DOPE composition as optimal, yielding robust mRNA expression. In primary neurons, RVG-functionalized PEGylated liposomes containing 10 mol% DOPE achieved gene expression levels comparable to those of a commercial transfection reagent at a 10:1 lipid:mRNA ratio. Notably, incorporating 0.1% w/w RVG significantly outperformed the commercial formulation, yielding >30% gene-delivery efficiency in primary neuronal cultures. In midbrain organoids, the optimized mRNA-loaded RVG-functionalized liposomes produced GFP mRNA expression overlapping with NeuN staining, demonstrating functional mRNA delivery and translation within three-dimensional neural tissue.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuron-targeted DOTAP: DOPE liposomes incorporating the RVG peptide represent a promising mRNA delivery system for neurological applications, achieving a favorable balance of potency, safety, and specificity and supporting transient gene modulation in the central nervous system.

title: Targeted Liposomal Nanocarriers for High-Efficiency Neuronal mRNA Delivery.

abstract: Magnetic liposomes (MLs) integrate the drug-loading capacity of liposomes with the magnetic responsiveness of nanoparticles, providing a theranostic platform that combines magnetic targeting, MRI contrast, magnetically triggered release, and magnetic hyperthermia. Preclinical studies have demonstrated these functions, but clinical translation has lagged behind the volume of published work. This review focuses on translation-critical issues in MLs. Structural comparisons (core-shell, embedded, conjugated) are discussed with attention to whether buffer-based structure-property relationships hold in biological fluids. Synthesis methods are compared for size uniformity, encapsulation efficiency, and scalability. Surface modification is assessed with emphasis on ligand density and on the protein corona as a variable modulating ligand accessibility, biomimetic coating function, and magnetothermal heating. Applications are reviewed, including imaging, targeted delivery, controlled release, combination therapy, and gene editing, with attention to thermal dose heterogeneity and the temporal coupling between heating and drug release. Clinical barriers are framed as specific methodological gaps in magnetic field standardization, sterilization, and in vitro-in vivo correlation.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable nucleic acid delivery, but formulation development remains empirical. Methods: We curated 1092 LNP formulations from 63 studies (2005-2025) and trained LightGBM models to predict particle size, encapsulation efficiency (EE%), and polydispersity index (PDI) using ionizable-lipid descriptors and formulation molar fractions. Results: Across random 80/20 splits (10 seeds), R2 values were 0.42 ± 0.06 for size (n = 850), 0.40 ± 0.16 for EE% (n = 523), and 0.43 ± 0.07 for PDI (n = 602), outperforming linear regression (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.002, 0.020, and 0.002). Combining structural and compositional features outperformed either subset. Lipid-identity holdout reduced R2 to 0.10 ± 0.38, 0.01 ± 0.28, and -0.39 ± 0.48 (exact SMILES) and to 0.10 ± 0.27, -0.19 ± 0.55, and -0.32 ± 0.41 (full InChIKey) for particle size, EE%, and PDI, respectively. Repeated scaffold-grouped cross-validation yielded R2 values of -0.16 ± 0.46, -0.27 ± 0.42, and -0.43 ± 1.04; paper-level holdout yielded -0.45 ± 0.31, -1.29 ± 1.74, and -0.86 ± 1.18. SHAP highlighted polar surface area, PEG-lipid fraction, and rotatable bonds. Conclusions: These findings support cautious interpolation within represented lipid chemistries but indicate poor transfer to unseen lipids, scaffolds, and studies.

abstract: Background: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive biliary tract malignancy with few targeted therapies. Though efforts have been made to identify actionable alterations and potential targeted strategies for GBC, its metabolic landscape and dependencies remain incompletely defined. Methods: We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of 27 paired GBC tissues and adjacent nontumor tissues and integrated these data with public transcriptomic cohorts and DepMap CRISPR dependency data to characterize metabolic alterations and vulnerabilities in GBC. Additionally, we analyzed a single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset to elucidate the potential biological role of glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase 2 (GPD2). Results: The multi-omic integration revealed obvious metabolic remodeling in GBC, including enhanced lipid biosynthesis and hexosamine biosynthetic pathway activity within the carbon metabolic network, together with polyamine accumulation. The DepMap-based dependency analysis prioritized solute carrier family 7 member 5 (SLC7A5) and succinate dehydrogenase complex iron sulfur subunit B (SDHB) as clinically relevant metabolic vulnerabilities. Among all the metabolites, glycerol 3-phosphate (Gro3P) was the most depleted, in parallel with the accumulation of dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) and the reciprocal expression of glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle (G3PS) enzyme genes, which was correlated with poor overall survival. The functional experiments showed that GPD2 knockdown unexpectedly enhanced primary tumor growth in a subcutaneous xenograft model. However, the scRNA-seq analysis and the cell migration assays linked GPD2 to a metastasis-associated epithelial state and tumor-cell motility. Conclusions: This study characterizes the metabolic landscape of GBC and reveals an uncoupled G3PS marked by Gro3P depletion. GPD2 expression is associated with a metastasis-related malignant epithelial state and poor prognosis, while GPD2 knockdown reduces cell migration in vitro. These findings warrant the further investigation of GPD2 in GBC progression, but its role in metastatic dissemination and its therapeutic implications remain to be established.

abstract: gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-Experiment-Assay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccine-related study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

abstract: Current lipid nanoparticle (LNP) optimisation and quality control frameworks suffer from a common limitation: they treat LNP formulations as morphologically uniform systems, obscuring single-particle structural heterogeneity. This opinion piece challenges the historical misconception that non-spherical, blebbed LNP architectures represent accidental manufacturing artefacts. Instead, we propose that the deliberate engineering of these non-equilibrium architectures represents a game-changing paradigm shift in RNA therapeutics. Consolidating emerging performance data, we argue that blebbed subpopulations yield enhancements in both in vitro and in vivo transfection potency. Blebbed LNPs may confer a particular advantage in difficult-to-transfect immune cell populations, thereby expanding their potential applications in immunotherapy and vaccine development. Mechanistically, this superior performance is proposed to be driven by the thermodynamic sequestration of ribonucleic acid (RNA) within the aqueous bleb compartment, shielding it from lipidation and degradation. Furthermore, we outline how bleb fraction can be prospectively engineered as a target product quality attribute using early-stage thermodynamic levers, specifically high-molarity kosmotropic buffers and delayed kinetic quenching under symmetric mixing conditions. To transition these architectures into a scalable clinical reality, we present a multi-parametric analytical roadmap combining automated, AI-enabled image analysis (LNP-MOD), cryogenic chemical mapping (Cryo-ToF-SIMS), high-resolution fractionation (AF4-SAXS), and single-particle loading quantification (NanoFCM, CLiC-ALEX). Crucially, we call for this analytical framework to be paired with biological validation across clinically relevant cell lines, prioritising immune cell populations to map subpopulation-specific trafficking. Ultimately, we advocate that specifying controlled morphological heterogeneity as a Critical Quality Attribute (CQA) managed during the manufacturing, storage and distribution stages is a true game-changer for the field. This framework has the potential to enable greater therapeutic potency, improve shelf-life, while also broadening global access to next-generation RNA medicine by reducing some of the logistical barriers often encountered in resource-limited settings.

abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines have emerged as a powerful vaccination platform, yet efficient and targeted delivery of mRNA to professional antigen-presenting cells (APCs) remains a major challenge. Here, we developed a dendritic cell (DC)-targeting virus-like particle (DVLP) platform for mRNA delivery by combining human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) Gag fused with the bacteriophage MS2 coat protein, which recognizes mRNA bearing MS2 stem-loop sequences and an engineered Sindbis virus glycoprotein mutant (SV-Gmt) that preferentially targets dendritic cells. African swine fever virus (ASFV) P30 was employed as a model antigen to evaluate platform performance. In vitro, SV-Gmt-pseudotyped VLPs encapsulating P30 mRNA (DVLP-P30) preferentially delivered antigen mRNA to dendritic cells compared with broad-tropic vesicular stomatitis virus G protein (VSV-G)-pseudotyped VLPs encapsulating P30 mRNA (VSV-G VLP-P30). In mice, vaccination with DVLP-P30 induced significantly higher P30-specific antibody responses than VSV-G VLP-P30. Enhanced humoral immunity was accompanied by increased frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ effector memory T cells, indicating improved generation of antigen-specific immune memory. Notably, DC-targeted mRNA delivery promoted stronger interferon-γ responses and increased IgG2a production, consistent with a Type 1 helper T cell (Th1)-skewed immune profile. Together, these findings demonstrate that DC-targeting VLPs function as effective mRNA carriers and enhance both the magnitude and quality of vaccine-induced immunity. This work establishes a versatile platform for targeted mRNA delivery and supports further development of DVLPs for prophylactic and therapeutic vaccination.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) therapeutics represent a transformative pharmacological paradigm in which the delivery vehicle, genetic payload, and expressed protein form a tightly coupled system. This multicomponent structure introduces nonlinear, multiscale dynamics that challenge traditional pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic frameworks, making quantitative modeling essential.
AREAS COVERED: This review provides a structured biological framework for mRNA-LNP therapeutics, detailing the key processes governing delivery, endosomal escape, mRNA stability, and translation, and highlighting their associated temporal and spatial scales, providing the key aspects to consider for modeling. Building on this foundation, we summarize mathematical modeling approaches, including pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK), and quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, used to represent these mechanisms. The literature was surveyed to identify representative preclinical and translational studies, focusing on model structure, assumptions, and their use in human projection and dose optimization.
EXPERT OPINION: Mathematical models are increasingly critical to interpret and predict mRNA therapeutic behavior, yet challenges remain in parameter identifiability, data availability, and model standardization. Future advances will depend on biologically grounded modeling frameworks, improved integration of mechanistic insight with quantitative approaches, and tighter coupling between experimental design and model development. These developments will support more efficient translation and enable precision medicine applications.

abstract: Therapy resistance in prostate cancer can emerge at different disease stages; castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is one clinically important state, and resistance to individual therapies may overlap but is not synonymous with CRPC. Metabolic reprogramming-including changes in glycolysis, de novo lipogenesis, glutamine metabolism, and mitochondrial homeostasis-has been implicated in prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance, although the strength of evidence varies across pathways and treatment settings. CircRNAs have been reported to modulate selected metabolic nodes in prostate cancer, although direct links between circRNA-associated metabolic changes and acquired therapy resistance are established only in a subset of studies. This review evaluates circRNAs as candidate regulators of selected metabolic processes in therapy-resistant prostate cancer. Mechanistically, individual circRNAs have been associated with selected metabolic changes through proposed miRNA-mediated interactions and, in some reports, peptide translation or protein scaffolding. These metabolic changes could, in principle, intersect with immunometabolic programmes such as lactate-associated suppression, lipid-linked macrophage states, and adenosine signalling; however, direct evidence that individual circRNAs control these immune-cell processes in CRPC remains limited, as detailed in the evidence tiers later in this review. Therapy-specific resistance networks are organised for enzalutamide/androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, PARP inhibitors and radiotherapy, distinguishing metabolism-dependent axes from signalling, mitotic, DNA-repair and exosome-propagated routes. Beyond mechanistic insights, circRNAs hold promise as non-invasive liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as druggable targets amenable to antisense oligonucleotide silencing, mimic delivery, and engineered circRNA vaccines. Major barriers to clinical translation include incomplete multi-therapy metabolic maps, sparse stage-resolved evidence across the hormone-sensitive→CRPC→neuroendocrine continuum, and unresolved delivery, safety, and regulatory challenges. Overall, current evidence supports circRNA-associated metabolic vulnerabilities as a promising preclinical research framework; however, circRNA-targeted metabolic interventions for therapy-resistant prostate cancer have not yet been clinically validated.

abstract: Represented by Inclisiran, small interfering RNA (siRNA)-based lipid-lowering therapy has reshaped long-term management of dyslipidaemia and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Existing reviews suffer from scattered evidence and inadequate mechanistic analysis, leaving many clinical uncertainties unresolved. This article summarises updated mechanisms, clinical profiles, real-world performance, safety and controversies of Inclisiran up to 2026, while identifying evidence gaps and research priorities. As an N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9)-targeting siRNA, Inclisiran induces hepatic PCSK9 silencing to sustainably lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)). Its semi-annual dosing improves adherence greatly, with favourable safety featuring low muscular toxicity and immunogenicity, yet its efficacy relies on functional low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). Current evidence fails to confirm definite cardiovascular benefits; pivotal trials are largely industry-sponsored, and interethnic efficacy variations remain unvalidated. Suitable for high-risk, statin-intolerant or non-adherent patients, Inclisiran requires independent trials, Asia-specific studies and long-term surveillance to advance precision lipid therapy.

title: Inclisiran: A RNA‑Interference‑Based Therapy for Dyslipidaemia: Mechanisms, Clinical Profile and Unresolved Clinical Controversies.

abstract: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is a hereditary small vessel disease caused by mutations in the NOTCH3 gene, primarily affecting vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. CADASIL variants often involve cysteine-altering mutations that disrupt the structure of the Notch3 extracellular domain (Notch3ECD), leading to granular osmiophilic material (GOM) deposition around vessel walls and causing subsequent pathological changes. Previous animal models have attempted to phenocopy the vascular and neurological pathologies of CADASIL, but yielded limited success in fully recapitulating the disease spectrum. To address this gap, we generated an independent Notch3 p.R545C CRISPR-edited knock-in mouse model, mirroring the prevalent East Asian-enriched human p.R544C variant. The Notch3R545C mice exhibited complex neurological deficits, including motor impairments, cognitive decline, and mood disturbances, alongside key features of arteriopathy such as Notch3ECD aggregates, GOM deposition, and impaired cerebrovascular reactivity. A distinct vasculopathy profile followed, characterized by intraluminal microthrombosis, hypoperfusion, blood-brain barrier disruption, and sporadic microbleeds. Our data support a vascular injury cascade driven by dysregulated vasoreactivity, resulting in progressive subcortical white matter (WM) degeneration and neuroinflammation with age. Moreover, our in vitro assays revealed that this atypical mutation significantly decreased ligand-binding efficiency and impaired ligand-induced signaling in trans, likely contributing to subtle pathological features beyond its neomorphic toxicity. Collectively, our mouse model demonstrates that vasoreactivity dysfunction precedes overt subcortical WM damage, while recapitulating dual vasculopathy of ischemic and hemorrhagic features. By identifying this physiological accuracy, our model provides a translational platform for mechanistic exploration and preclinical therapeutic development.

title: Vasoreactivity dysfunction precedes extensive white matter damage: insights from a Notch3 R545C knock-in mouse model for CADASIL.

abstract: Although the FLT3 inhibitor gilteritinib is initially effective in patients with FLT3-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML), patients invariably relapse within months of treatment. Gilteritinib resistance is commonly driven by the emergence of NRAS mutations and a shift toward a more monocytic cell state. We hypothesized that directly targeting and depleting NRAS protein would reverse these adaptive differentiation changes and restore therapeutic sensitivity. To test this, we used a mutation-agnostic antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) to selectively knock down NRAS expression across gilteritinib-resistant AML cell lines, in vivo cell line-derived xenografts, and primary patient samples. NRAS ASO successfully resensitized gilteritinib-resistant cells with multiple distinct NRAS mutations, displaying superior efficacy compared with downstream MEK inhibition. This therapeutic efficacy was independent of NRAS-mutant variant allele frequency, suggesting that wild-type NRAS may also contribute to resistance. Comprehensive multiomics profiling (transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics) revealed that NRAS knockdown consistently reversed the monocytic phenotype, shifting cells back toward a more primitive cell state. Monocytic differentiation and NRAS mutations are established drivers of resistance to diverse targeted regimens in AML, including FLT3, IDH, and BCL2 inhibitors. Therefore, we also tested venetoclax-resistant primary cells with NRAS mutations. Resistant cells were resensitized to venetoclax after NRAS knockdown, suggesting that NRAS knockdown may be more broadly applicable for overcoming monocytic cell state and drug resistance in AML.

title: NRAS knockdown reverses monocytic cell state and resensitizes resistant FLT3-AML cells to gilteritinib.

abstract: LIM and SH3 domain protein 1 (LASP1) is a critical regulator of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression; however, its downstream effectors and underlying regulatory mechanisms remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify adaptor-related protein complex 1 subunit mu 2 (AP1M2) as a key downstream effector of LASP1 and uncover a regulatory mechanism by which LASP1 maintains AP1M2 protein stability in CRC. Mechanistically, LASP1 directly interacts with AP1M2 and competes with the E3 ubiquitin ligase SMURF1 for AP1M2 binding, thereby suppressing SMURF1-mediated K48-linked polyubiquitination of AP1M2 at lysine 14 (K14) and preventing its proteasomal degradation. Functionally, AP1M2 stabilization promotes aberrant E-cadherin sorting, activates Wnt signaling, and enhances CRC cell proliferation and tumorigenesis. Genetic deletion of Lasp1 in Azoxymethane/Dithiothreitol (AOM/DSS)-induced CRC models and LASP1 knockdown in xenograft models suppress the LASP1-AP1M2-E-cadherin axis and tumor growth in vivo. Furthermore, a cyclic RGD-modified lipid nanoparticle (cRGD-LNP)-based antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) delivery system was developed to efficiently silence LASP1 expression and suppress patient-derived xenograft (PDX) tumor growth. Collectively, this study identifies the LASP1-AP1M2-E-cadherin axis as a critical driver of CRC progression and provides a nano-delivery strategy with clinical translational potential for precision targeting of this axis.

abstract:
The goal of this clinical trial is to assess the safety and tolerability of a virus replicon particle (VRP) encapsulated saRNA encoding IL-12 when injected into in head and neck cancer patients. The main questions being addressed are:

The safety and tolerability of intratumoral (IT) injections of VRP-encapsulated saRNA encoding IL-12 (VLPONC-01)

The tumor response to IT injections of VLPONC-01

The tumor response due to the combination of IT injections of VLPONC-01 and system IV administration of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) treatment

Researchers will compare neoadjuvant pembrolizumab alone to the combination therapy to see if the combination enhances tumor responses.

institutions.label: Stanford University

description:
The study is an Open label, Phase I study to determine the safety of IT injected VLPONC-01 as a therapeutic agent in subjects with non-resectable and resectable Head and Neck Cancer Squamous Cell Carcinomas (HCSCC), and secondarily to assess pathologic response and radiological response (assessed by RECIST 1.1 criteria) in the primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Researchers also will explore tumor microenvironment changes in cytokine levels and cellular responses.

There will be three distinct cohorts enrolling sequentially:

Cohort A: Researchers will enroll unresectable or recurrent/metastatic head and neck cancer with at least 1 injectable tumor not scheduled for tumor resection surgery who will receive four doses of VLPONC-01.

Cohort C: Researchers will enroll HCSCC patients scheduled for tumor resection surgery who will receive four doses of VLPONC-1 and two doses of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab or only two doses of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab prior to tumor resection surgery.

abstract: High-dose vitamin C has re-emerged as a promising metabolic strategy for treating acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but its use in combination with targeted therapies remains underexplored. Here, we identified BCL-2 as a top sensitizer to vitamin C, using unbiased CRISPR-Cas9 drug-target screening of MOLM-13 cells. Combination therapy with vitamin C and the BCL-2 inhibitor lisaftoclax (APG-2575) produced a synergistic effect that concurrently triggered two distinct, pharmacologically separable cell-death programs: caspase-dependent apoptosis and heme oxygenase 1 (HMOX1)-dependent ferroptosis. The combination therapy suppressed leukemic progression and prolonged survival in both cell line-derived and patient-derived xenograft models, with acceptable tolerability. Mechanistically, a second CRISPR screen targeting transcription factors identified IKAROS family zinc finger 1 (IKZF1) loss as a key resistance driver that attenuated synergy, downregulated Bim, and derepressed AXL expression through increased chromatin accessibility at an IKZF1-bound AXL regulatory region. Genetic AXL depletion or pharmacological inhibition with R428 partially restored sensitivity in IKZF1-depleted cells. These findings demonstrated that vitamin C-APG-2575 combination therapy exerts its effect through a dual apoptotic-ferroptotic cell death mechanism. Additionally, the IKZF1-AXL axis was identified as a therapeutically actionable resistance pathway in the context of AML treatment.

abstract: Hereditary tyrosinemia type I (HT1) is a severe autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase (FAH) gene, leading to progressive and often fatal liver injury. Currently, no curative therapy is available. Nitisinone (NTBC), an inhibitor of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPD), is the standard treatment for HT1; however, its efficacy during lactation has not been systematically evaluated in large animal models. In this study, a FAH knockout (FAH-KO) rabbit model was generated using CRISPR/Cas9 genome-editing technology and was shown to faithfully recapitulate the characteristic hepatic and renal pathological features of human HT1. Using this translationally relevant model, we compared different NTBC administration strategies. Combined breastfeeding and oral NTBC treatment achieved a survival rate of 87.5% over a 3-month observation period, whereas all offspring receiving NTBC exclusively through breast milk died within 15 days (P < 0.01). Under sustained NTBC maintenance therapy, FAH-KO rabbits survived, exhibited normal growth and development, reproduced successfully, and established stable Mendelian inheritance. Furthermore, we validated an adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based metabolic reprogramming strategy. Hepatic portal vein delivery of HPD-targeting RNA interference via a self-complementary AAV vector achieved liver-specific HPD knockdown. A single scAAV-HPD administration rescued the lethal phenotype, restored liver and kidney biochemical parameters to near-normal levels, and supported sustained survival. Collectively, this study provides a robust HT1 rabbit model and proof-of-concept evidence for a long-lasting AAV-mediated therapeutic strategy.

abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing has transformed biomedical research and is advancing toward clinical translation. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) offers improved precision in guide RNA design, off-target prediction, and delivery optimization. This review synthesizes recent advances in CRISPR-Cas9 for medical applications, covering core mechanisms, engineered variants, base and prime editors, and therapeutic applications including CAR T-cell and CAR-NK engineering, genetic disorders, infectious diseases, and regenerative medicine. Delivery strategies are evaluated with emphasis on AI-driven optimization. AI applications are highlighted across deep learning architectures for guide RNA design, AI-designed nucleases such as OpenCRISPR-1, structure-guided and AI-assisted design of compact high-fidelity SaCas9 variants, reinforcement learning for pipeline optimization, and roles in CAR T-cell therapy and safety assessment. Safety challenges are examined, including off-target effects, chromosomal rearrangements, immunogenicity, and regulatory concerns. Future directions emphasize multi-scale modeling, explainable AI, clinical validation, and integration with synthetic biology, single-cell sequencing, organoids, and nanomaterials. The convergence of AI and CRISPR-Cas9 holds substantial potential for personalized medicine.

title: AI-Enhanced CRISPR-Cas9 Therapeutics: Advances in Precision, Safety, and Delivery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). In a randomized placebo-controlled trial in patients with established cardiovascular disease, pelacarsen did not reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to placebo. We further investigated the association of pelacarsen treatment with cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: We report the association of pelacarsen treatment with a primary composite end point of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. Analyses included on-treatment, uninterrupted treatment, total primary end point events (first and recurrent events), landmark analyses classified by changes in and achieved lipoprotein(a) at 3 months, and key subgroups including baseline lipoprotein(a), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), and time from qualifying event to enrollment.
RESULTS: For participants on treatment, a primary end point occurred in 434 participants (10.4%) randomly assigned to placebo and 380 participants (9.1%) assigned to pelacarsen (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.12). When evaluating participants with uninterrupted treatment, a primary end point event occurred in 167 participants (11.0%) in the pelacarsen group and 204 participants (10.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34). When evaluating total primary end point events, there were 644 events in the pelacarsen group and 646 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.14). In landmark analyses evaluating participants alive and free of the composite end point at 3 months, when compared to placebo there was no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point either in participants with reduction in lipoprotein(a) greater than or equal to the median (170 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.29) or in participants who achieved lipoprotein(a) lower than or equal to the median (69.5 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.29). There was also no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point in any of the evaluated key subgroups including classification by median baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, high-sensitivity CRP, or time from qualifying cardiovascular disease to enrollment.
CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen was not associated with a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when evaluated by treatment exposure, changes in or achieved lipoprotein(a) levels at 3 months, considering total events, or within subgroups of baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, or high-sensitivity CRP levels.

title: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

abstract: Cancer remains a leading global mortality cause, driven by complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that facilitate progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Cytokines form the central regulatory network governing TME intercellular communication, exerting highly context-dependent pro- and anti-tumorigenic effects. Dysregulated cytokine signaling drives chronic inflammation and immunosuppression, limiting durable therapeutic responses. While cytokine-based immunotherapies show clinical potential, their widespread use is hindered by poor stability, rapid clearance, limited specificity, and dose-limiting toxicities. Advances in nanomedicine offer innovative solutions by improving cytokine pharmacokinetics, tumor-selective delivery, and spatiotemporally controlled release. Beyond passive delivery, engineered nanoplatforms act as active modulators of the tumor immune ecosystem, remodeling cytokine networks to restore antitumor immunity. Nanotechnology interventions effectively regulate key signaling pathways- including JAK/STAT, TGF-β/SMAD, NF-κB, MAPK/ERK, and PI3K/AKT- disrupting pathological feedback mechanisms and crosstalk. Furthermore, localized cytokine delivery, gene silencing, mRNA therapeutics, and CRISPR-enabled genome engineering are expanding precision immunotherapy. Despite significant translational challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, biological barriers, immunogenicity, and manufacturing complexity emerging biomimetic and personalized nanoplatforms offer promising avenues for precise immune modulation and biomarker-guided patient stratification. Literature searches were conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect (with Google Scholar for citation tracking) covering peer-reviewed publications from 2003 to 2026.

title: Cytokine networks in the tumor microenvironment: nanotherapeutic modulation of immune-cell communication and signaling networks.

abstract: While clinical translation of messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technologies has redefined vaccinology, the development of potent platforms against complex bacterial pathogens is often limited by the transient expression kinetics and rapid clearance of encoded antigens. One well established approach to enhance immunogenicity is the fusion of an Fc fragment to an antigen. However, the mechanism of Fc-mediated potentiation within mRNA-LNP systems is, yet, undefined, specifically regarding the necessity of receptor-mediated interactions. Here, we demonstrate that an mRNA-LNP vaccine, encoding an Fc-fragment fused to the Yersinia pestis F1 antigen, drives robust, protective immunity against the lethal bubonic plague by functioning as a pharmacokinetic stabilizer. Through systematic architectural design, variation of Fc isotypes, species-matched scaffolding, and glycosylation profiling, we reveal that Fc-integration extends systemic antigen bioavailability by over 300-fold, providing a sustained kinetic window for immune priming. Remarkably, immunogenicity is preserved in Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-deficient mice, as well as with a reduced FcγR-binding Fc variant, suggesting that protective immunity is independent of classical FcγR engagement in this model. These findings decouple Fc-mediated enhancement from receptor-mediated interactions, identifying structural stabilization and prolonged persistence as the primary drivers of efficacy in mRNA-LNP vaccines. Altogether, our results provide a mechanistic framework for the design of high-potency mRNA vaccines through engineered protein stability.

abstract: A biomimetic magnetic nanocarrier was developed to facilitate the targeted delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 components to breast cancer cells, with the aim of improving tumor-directed gene delivery and reducing nonspecific distribution to healthy tissues. The effective delivery vector for partial WT1 disruption consists of a superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) core loaded with a genome-editing plasmid. The SPION is wrapped in a red blood cell membrane functionalized with the nuclear- and cancer cell-targeting aptamer AS1411. Findings from cytotoxicity assays and western blot analyses validated the effectiveness of this delivery system. Furthermore, fluorescence imaging and flow cytometry demonstrated enhanced GFP reporter expression in 4T1 cells treated with PSMA compared with the nontargeted formulation, suggesting improved functional plasmid delivery. In vivo investigations revealed substantial tumor-growth inhibition following PSMA administration, while ex vivo fluorescence imaging showed enhanced tumor-associated GFP reporter signals compared with the nontargeted formulation. Moreover, the diagnostic potential of the synthesized SPION-CRISPR/Cas9 plasmid/membrane/aptamer complex was evaluated using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which revealed enhanced contrast at the tumor site. Overall, this platform demonstrates potential for tumor-directed plasmid delivery and MRI-based imaging, although further studies are required to establish reproducible WT1-editing efficiency, long-term safety, and therapeutic specificity.

title: Biomimetic magnetic nanocarriers for theranostic CRISPR/Cas9 delivery: targeting WT1 in a murine model of breast cancer.

abstract: Targeted modulation of microglial activation with siRNA in neuroinflammatory diseases presents a compelling therapeutic strategy by enabling precise gene silencing while preserving beneficial immune responses. However, the immune-sensitive nature of microglia creates unique barriers to safe and efficient siRNA delivery. Dual pH- and redox-responsive polycationic nanogels with tunable molecular architectures are developed to overcome these barriers, enabling spatiotemporal delivery and intracellular degradation. Varying hydrophilic and hydrophobic monomer ratios tunes nanogel molecular architecture to control particle size, pH-responsive behavior, and therapeutic release. Disulfide crosslinkers enable selective degradation of polymer networks into fragments at intracellular glutathione levels, enabling controlled release and intracellular degradation. Increased hydrophobic composition yields smaller hydrodynamic size, optimal pH swelling profile for endosomal escape, and surface charge shifts that balance membrane disruption and biocompatibility. Degradation studies confirm redox-responsive crosslinks selective fragmentation at intracellular glutathione levels. Systematic siRNA loading studies demonstrate electrostatic interactions dominate, achieving high loading efficiency. Release studies mimicking intracellular environmental shifts confirm the spatiotemporal siRNA delivery from dual-responsive nanogels. Nanogels demonstrate first-pass cytocompatibility (MTS and LDH assays) with microglia at therapeutic concentrations. Both formulations achieve intracellular accumulation of carboxyfluorescein (FAM)-labelled siRNA in microglia, with higher efficacy for the more hydrophobic formulation. Future work will investigate the platform's innate immune response in microglia and functional knockdown of disease-relevant genes with target specific siRNA to modulate microglia's neuroinflammatory response. Collectively, these dual-responsive nanogels provide a foundational rational design framework for vectors that balance biosafety and delivery efficacy for siRNA therapies to microglia for targeting neuroinflammation.

abstract: Autosomal dominant inherited retinal dystrophies (AD-IRDs) constitute a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of disorders in Japan, including retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and the disease category of "macular dystrophies" caused by numerous pathogenic variants across more than 25 genes. Although AD-IRDs represent a smaller proportion of IRDs when compared with autosomal recessive or X-linked forms, their clinical significance is substantial owing to high variable penetrance, marked intrafamilial variability, and the frequent presence of late-onset or mild phenotypes that remain underdiagnosed.The introduction of next-generation sequencing (NGS) enabled multigene testing and improved diagnostic yields in RP cohorts, with subsequent advances increasing detection rates to approximately 45%, particularly for AD-IRDs. More recently, IRD-specific variant interpretation frameworks have further enhanced diagnostic accuracy and nationwide genomic integration.These advances have clarified the genetic spectrum of AD-IRDs in Japan, with recurrent pathogenic variants in hotspots identified in RHO, RP1, RP1L1, PRPH2, and GUCY2D as major contributors. In parallel, deep phenotyping using multimodal retinal imaging, electrophysiology, and refined genotype-phenotype correlation analyses has revealed population-specific variant distributions associated with characteristic clinical patterns in Japanese cohorts. In addition, emerging therapeutic approaches have now been developed, including gene editing, allele-specific suppression, antisense oligonucleotides, RNA editing, and regenerative cell transplantation strategies.This review summarizes the large-scale cohort studies, molecular functions, phenotypes, and ethnic characteristics of Japanese AD-IRDs and discusses future directions toward precision medicine.

abstract: Despite wide investigation on gene editing, intracellular delivery of CRISPR ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes still remains a major barrier to therapeutic applications. Here, we developed a non-cationic, hyaluronate-functionalized gold nanoparticle (HA-AuNP) platform for PLK1-targeted cancer therapy with Cas12a-crRNA RNPs. The sequential changes in particle size, optical response, and surface charge supported the nanoparticle assembly. Comparative cellular fluorescence measurements and free-HA competitive tests supported the HA receptor mediated cellular uptake. Intracellular imaging showed the redistribution of labeled cargo relative to LysoTracker-positive compartments and calcein redistribution imaging supported the vesicular membrane permeabilization. In HeLa cells, the PLK1-targeting formulation induced ca. 8% target-site indels, reduced PLK1 protein abundance, and decreased cellular metabolic activity. Following intratumoral administration, tumor target-site indels were detected, PLK1 protein abundance was reduced, and tumor growth was suppressed in HeLa xenograft model mice. Hematological, biochemical, cytokine, and histological assessments supported the tolerability under the tested conditions. These findings provide a locoregional proof of concept for non-cationic HA-AuNP-mediated CRISPR RNP delivery and PLK1-directed cancer therapy.

title: Hyaluronate-gold nanoparticle-CRISPR complexes for targeted PLK1 gene editing cancer therapy.

abstract: Genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems are chemogenetic tools that utilize small molecules to regulate protein association, higher-order assembly, and dissociation. Over the past three decades, an expanding repertoire of these systems has transformed the study of protein function and cellular signaling by enabling rapid, reversible, and tunable manipulation of protein localization, assembly, activity, and downstream physiological processes. As these technologies advance from experimental tools toward therapeutic applications, their translational potential depends not only on molecular switch performance but also on the properties of the chemical inducer and engineered protein components. In this review, we summarize the major classes and design principles of representative genetically encoded chemically controlled proximity systems, with particular emphasis on the pharmacological determinants that define their therapeutic operating window, including pharmacodynamic orthogonality, pharmacokinetics, tissue exposure, endogenous target engagement, and clinical readiness. We also examine how the biological origin and engineering of the chemogenetic modules influence immunogenicity and long-term compatibility. We further discuss exemplary applications, including pharmacological control of CAR-T cell activity, programmed cell death, CRISPR-based genome and epigenome engineering, and on-demand secretion of therapeutic proteins. Finally, we consider the delivery and coordinated expression of chemically regulated protein components as major remaining barriers to therapeutic implementation and highlight clinically compatible inducers, compact and minimally immunogenic protein modules, de novo protein design, and advances in viral and nonviral delivery as promising directions toward more reliable and pharmacologically tractable chemically controlled therapies.

abstract: mRNA-based cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising platform for therapeutic cancer immunotherapy because of their ability to encode tumor-associated antigens, tumor-specific antigens, and patient-specific neoantigens and to induce antigen-specific immune responses. Their flexible and cell-free manufacturing enables rapid adaptation and facilitates the development of personalized vaccines based on individual tumor mutations and HLA profiles. However, the clinical translation of mRNA-based cancer vaccines remains challenging because of difficulties in neoantigen identification, maintaining mRNA stability, achieving efficient intracellular and tissue-specific delivery and endosomal escape, optimizing antigen expression, and overcoming tumor heterogeneity, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Advances in mRNA engineering, including sequence optimization, modified nucleosides, cap and UTR optimization, and lipid nanoparticle-based delivery, have improved RNA stability, cellular uptake, antigen expression, and immune activation in various experimental and clinical settings. This review discusses the principles of mRNA-based cancer vaccines, strategies for neoantigen identification and vaccine development, mRNA production and formulation, nanoparticle-mediated delivery, major challenges affecting stability, targeting, expression, and immune stimulation, and emerging clinical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on personalized neoantigen vaccines and combination approaches with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Continued integration of RNA engineering, nanotechnology, computational antigen prediction, and precision immunotherapy may enable more effective and clinically adaptable mRNA-based cancer vaccines.

description: This is a blinded, two-arm randomised study to determine the safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity of a fourth dose of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines in Australia in adults 18 years or older who have received their third dose of COVID-19 vaccine at least six months previously. Participants will be randomised to receive either bivalent Moderna (mRNA-1273.214) or Novavax. A separate non-randomised control arm (no vaccine given), frequency matched by age to the vaccine groups will also be enrolled for comparison. A total of 200 participants per group will be recruited.

outcomes.description: Serum samples collected at 28-days post booster vaccination from the two intervention groups will be evaluated for SARS-CoV-2 specific IgG antibodies using the commercial Euroimmun S1 IgG ELISA. Data will be reported as binding antibody units/mL and presented as geometric mean concentration and 95% confidence intervals
outcomes.measure: SARS-CoV-2 Specific Immunoglobulin (Ig)G Antibodies at 28-days Post Booster Vaccination

outcomes.description: Questionnaire to document solicited reactions is developed specifically for this study. Data will be reported as the proportion of participants who report by each intervention arm. Solicited reactions such as pain, tenderness, erythema/redness, induration/swelling, fever, nausea/vomiting, headache, fatigue/malaise, myalgia, arthralgia will be collected from the participants 7 days post-vaccination. Reactogenicity was graded on a 0-4 scale: Grade 0 = no symptom; Grade 1 = mild and does not interfere with activity; Grade 2 = moderate or requiring repeated non-narcotic analgesia; Grade 3 = severe, limiting or preventing daily activity; Grade 4 = potentially life-threatening, requiring ER visit or hospitalisation.
outcomes.measure: Total Incidence of Solicited Reactions (Systemic and Local)
outcomes.time_frame: Total incidence of solicited reactions will be measured for 7 days post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Serum samples collected at baseline (pre booster), 28 days, 6,12, 18, 24, and 30 months post booster vaccination from the two intervention groups and the control group will be evaluated for SARS-CoV-2 specific IgG antibodies using the commercial Euroimmun S1 IgG ELISA . Data will be reported as binding antibody units/mL and presented as geometric mean concentration and 95% confidence intervals
outcomes.measure: SARS-CoV-2 Specific IgG Antibodies at Baseline (Pre Booster), and 6,12 and 18 Months Post Booster Vaccination
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 6-months,12-months and 18-months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Neutralising antibody levels will be measured using the GenScript® cPass sVNT, which reports inhibition relative to a positive control. Results are expressed as concentrations (U/mL) and summarised as geometric mean concentrations (GMCs) with 95% CIs.
outcomes.measure: SARS-CoV-2 Specific Neutralising Antibodies Measured by Surrogate Virus Neutralization Test (sVNT)
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 28 days, 6,12, 18, 24, and 30 months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: A subset of samples (20%) from all timepoints will be assessed using a SARS-CoV-2 microneutralisation assay to both the wild type (vaccine) strain and for two SARS-CoV-2 Variants of concern. Neutralizing antibody will be reported as endpoint titre.
outcomes.measure: SARS-CoV-2 Specific Neutralising Antibodies at Baseline (Pre Booster), 28 Days and 6, 12 and 18 Months Post Booster Vaccination Measured by SARS-CoV-2 Microneutralisation Assay
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 6,12 and 18-months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Interferon gamma (IFNγ) concentrations as a measurement of cellular immunity will be assessed on a subset (50%) of the participants from each group. QuantiFERON Human IFN-γ SARS-CoV-2 (Qiagen) will be used to stimulate IFN-γ production in whole blood and then IFN-γ production will be measured using Enzyme-Linked ImmunoSorbent Assay (ELISA). Data will be presented as geometric mean concentration (GMC) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).
outcomes.measure: Interferon Gamma (IFNγ) Concentrations in International Units (IU)/mL
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), Day 28, 6-months and 12-months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: IFNγ producing cells as a measurement of cellular immunity will be assessed on a subset (50%) of the participants from each group. IFN-γ Enzyme-Linked ImmunoSpot (Elispot) assay will be performed on isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) stimulated with SARS-CoV-2 specific peptides. Data will be reported as number of IFNγ producing cells/million and presented using means and 95% confidence intervals.
outcomes.measure: Number of IFNγ Producing Cells/Million PBMCs
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 6, 12 and 18-months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Frequency of cytokine-expressing T cells will be assessed on a subset (50%) of participants using Flow cytometry (intracellular staining) on PBMCs samples stimulated with SARS-CoV-2 specific peptides. Data will be reported as frequency (%) of cytokine-expressing T cells presented as means and 95% CI.
outcomes.measure: Frequency of Cytokine-expressing T Cells
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 6, 12 and 18 -months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Cytokine concentrations following PBMCs stimulation will be assessed on a subset (50%) of participants using multiplex cytokine assays. Data will be reported as cytokine concentrations in pg/ml and presented as GMC and 95% CI.
outcomes.measure: Cytokine Concentrations Following PBMCs Stimulation
outcomes.time_frame: Baseline (pre booster), 6, 12 and 18-months post booster vaccination

outcomes.description: Unsolicited adverse events were collected for 28 days post-booster. Results are reported as the number and percentage of randomised participants in each arm who experienced an unsolicited AE.
outcomes.measure: Incidence of Unsolicited Adverse Events (AE)

outcomes.description: Participants with medically attended AE will be collected for 3 months post booster vaccination. Data will be presented as number of medically attended adverse events. Serious adverse events (SAEs) are reported separately.
outcomes.measure: Incidence of Medically Attended Adverse Events (AE)

outcomes.description: Serious adverse events (SAEs) were collected throughout the 24-month follow-up period after booster vaccination. Data are reported as the number of SAEs occurring in each randomised arm.
outcomes.measure: Incidence of Serious Adverse Events (SAE)

outcomes.description: SARS-CoV-2 infections were recorded throughout the 24-month follow-up period based on participant self-report of a positive RAT or PCR test. Data are reported as the number of infections occurring in each study arm during this period
outcomes.measure: SARS-CoV-2 Infections

abstract: Since its discovery, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) has revolutionized biomedical science and engineering with its ability to recognize and edit gene sequences with high specificity and precision. Despite the growing interest in using these capabilities to address environmental and sustainability challenges, the broader potential of CRISPR in environmental systems remains unexplored relative to its biomedical applications. Here, we provide a critical perspective on the emerging use of CRISPR for pollution management, ecological conservation, and environmental monitoring. Rather than viewing CRISPR solely as a gene-editing or biosensing technology, we consider both capabilities together to examine how advances in CRISPR engineering can translate into practical environmental solutions. We highlight the fundamental principles behind CRISPR-based editing and sensing and evaluate the challenges that constrain their transition from proof-of-concept experiments to field deployment, including off-target effects, delivery methods, ecological risks, and low sensitivity. Addressing these hurdles requires a multifaceted approach that integrates emerging technologies such as reversible CRISPR technology, amplification and cascade reactions, and machine learning, with strict regulatory oversight and rigorous risk assessments. This perspective identifies critical strengths, weaknesses, and research priorities for advancing CRISPR from laboratory technology toward robust tools for environmental applications.

abstract: This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled Phase 2 study to determine the efficacy and safety of NWRD09 administered by intramuscular (IM) injection in adult women with histologically confirmed cervical high grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 \[CIN2\] or grade 3 \[CIN3\]) associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) 16.
description:
This is a Phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of NWRD09 in patients with HPV16 positive cervical high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL). Eligible participants are randomized to receive either NWRD09 or the corresponding placebo.

Participants will receive intramuscular injections of either NWRD09 or matching placebo at the corresponding dose at weeks 0, 2, 4, and 12 (a total of 4 doses).

Efficacy evaluations at Week 24 will include histopathological biopsy and HPV testing.

abstract: PRE-EMPT will assemble a cohort of 150 participants from three populations (low risk, intermediate risk, and high risk for self-harm). We will obtain clinical assessments, structural and functional MRI utilizing tasks pioneered by our team to assess cognitive control (CC) and emotion regulation (ER), and peripheral circular RNA (circRNA) levels to characterize the molecular brain states associated with behavioral risk. The clinical, imaging, and transcriptomic data will be fused and jointly analyzed to increase the accuracy of our risk prediction models. PRE-EMPT in three separate Aims will then prospectively assess three promising and innovative interventions for their potential to reduce suicidal ideation and alter activity in key neural networks: 1) neurofeedback (NF) using real-time fMRI with simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), 2) a form of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) called accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) with dose optimization through electric field modeling; and 3) psilocybin assisted therapy (PSI), with flexible dosing plan to maximize the depth of psychedelic experience. These therapies were chosen based on our team's prior work in all three interventions demonstrating rapid action and large effects.

abstract:
The Investigators have demonstrated in preclinical studies that RNA liposomes activate APCs, induce antigen-specific T cell immunity, and can supplant DCs in a cell therapy model for HGG and have shown feasibility and activity of this approach in preclinical models and in canine patients with a spontaneous malignant glioma. In one arm of this study, the investigators investigate the safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccines in pediatric patients with recurrent pHGG.

The investigators have also shown that intravenous administration of tumor mRNA loaded lipid particles (LPs) localizes primarily to lung, transfect antigen presenting cells (APCs) and lead to an activated T cell response for induction of anti-tumor immunity. In contrast to other formulations, RNA-LPs recruit multiple arms of the immune system (i.e. innate/adaptive), and remodel the systemic/intratumoral immune milieu, which remain potent barriers for vaccine, cellular, and checkpoint inhibiting immunotherapies. The investigators have already demonstrated safety of RNA-LPs in acute/chronic murine toxicity studies, and in client-owned canine trial.

In this study, the investigators will investigate the manufacturing feasibility, safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccine in patients with recurrent pulmonary or unresectable osteosarcoma and recurrent pHGG.

abstract: Transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) drives Foxp3 induction and peripheral regulatory T (pTreg) cell differentiation, yet how pTreg cell commitment is restricted under suboptimal TGF-β remains unclear. Through sequential genome-wide in vitro and sub-library in vivo CRISPR-Cas9 screens, we identified Zmynd8 as a key negative regulator of pTreg cell differentiation. Zmynd8 deficiency enhanced induced Treg cell differentiation in vitro, particularly at low TGF-β concentrations. In vivo, loss of ZMYND8 skewed T cell fate toward pTreg cells at the expense of Th17 and Th1 populations. Mechanistically, ZMYND8 forms co-repressor complexes with NuRD, LSD1, and KDM5 demethylases. TGF-β-SMAD2/3 signaling recruits these complexes to the Foxp3 super-enhancer to restrain enhancer activity and Foxp3 expression, establishing an epigenetic threshold for pTreg cell commitment. This intrinsic counter-regulatory arm within TGF-β signaling is conserved in human CD4+ T cells. Zmynd8-deficient induced Treg cells showed improved lineage stability and superior control of graft-versus-host disease, suggesting therapeutic potential for ZMYND8 modulation.

abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapy offers a programmable route to melanoma treatment, but its translation is limited by nuclease degradation, off-target biodistribution and endolysosomal trapping. Here we report a glutathione (GSH)/pH dual-responsive mRNA nanocomplex (mRNA-NC) fabricated by one-pot in situ polymerization of N-(3-aminopropyl)methacrylamide (APMA), 1-vinylimidazole (VI), N,N'-bis(acryloyl)cystamine (BACA), and 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) on the mRNA template. At an N/P ratio of 40, the carrier reached an encapsulation efficiency of 92.7 ± 2.1% and a loading capacity of 87.4 ± 3.2 μg mg-1, forming monodisperse particles of 126.4 ± 7.2 nm (polydispersity index, PDI, 0.14). The zwitterionic corona limited plasma protein adsorption to 12.6 ± 1.5 μg mg-1 (4.6-fold lower than jetPEI/mRNA), kept hemolysis at 0.8 ± 0.2%, and extended the serum half-life of the mRNA to ≈27.4 h, roughly 9-fold longer than naked mRNA. Release was gated by both triggers: 86.5 ± 3.7% of the cargo was released within 8 h under 10 mM GSH, whereas leakage under physiological conditions remained ≤ 12%; in a 4 h matrix, pH 5.5 plus 10 mM GSH released 85 ± 6.8% versus 12 ± 1.5% at pH 7.4 without GSH. In B16F10 cells, the nanocomplex was taken up in a dose- and energy-dependent manner, entered the lysosomal compartment, and escaped over time in a manner consistent with imidazole-mediated proton-sponge buffering (a hypothesis; intralysosomal pH was not measured directly), producing a peak firefly luciferase (FLuc) expression of 56,140 ± 3280 RLU mg-1 protein at 24 h, about 1.5-fold higher than jetPEI/mRNA, with 93.6 ± 3.9% cell viability and 6.7 ± 1.2% lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. In B16F10-bearing albino C57BL/6 mice, a single intravenous dose produced tumor-dominant bioluminescence (peak 5.7 × 106 photons s-1 at 6 h), a tumor enrichment index of 1.22 ± 0.18 (vs 0.31 ± 0.03 for jetPEI/mRNA) and 2.42 × 107 FLuc mRNA copies μg-1 tumor RNA at 12 h, while all 7-day safety indicators remained at phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) levels. These results demonstrate that a single zwitterionic nanocomplex can integrate stealth, dual-triggered release, and endosomal escape for safe, tumor-enriched mRNA delivery. While this study focuses on delivery performance and reporter gene expression, it lays a solid foundation for future therapeutic applications with functional mRNA.
